questions.stem: What is the primary function of the Nigeria Customs Service?

options.text: To collect taxes on goods entering and leaving Nigeria.
To regulate the prices of goods in the market.
To manage the Nigerian stock exchange.

questions.explanation: The primary function of the Nigeria Customs Service is to collect taxes on goods entering and leaving the country, ensuring compliance with trade regulations.

distractorRationale.a: Option b is incorrect because the Customs Service does not regulate prices.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is incorrect; providing loans is not a function of the Customs Service.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect as the Customs Service does not manage the stock exchange.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes customs duty?

options.text: A tax on goods produced within the country.
A tax on goods imported or exported.

questions.explanation: Customs duty is specifically a tax on goods that are imported or exported across international borders.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect; that describes excise duty.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is incorrect because customs duty is a tax, not a shipping fee.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect as customs duty does not apply to services.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between customs duty and excise duty?

options.text: Customs duty is for imported goods, while excise duty is for domestic goods.
Customs duty is higher than excise duty.
Excise duty is only paid by manufacturers.
There is no difference; they are the same.

questions.explanation: The main difference is that customs duty applies to goods entering the country, while excise duty applies to goods produced domestically.

distractorRationale.a: Option b is incorrect; the rates vary and are not necessarily related.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is misleading; excise duty can be paid by consumers as well.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect; customs and excise duties serve different purposes.
